jp: 隣[となり]の席[せき]の友達[ともだち]が私[わたし]に消[け]しゴムを{くれました|gv-kureru}。
en: The friend at the next desk gave me an eraser.
why: The giver is a friend and the receiver is me, so it is くれる.

jp: 同僚[どうりょう]が私[わたし]に出張[しゅっちょう]のお土産[みやげ]を{くれました|gv-kureru}。
en: A colleague gave me a souvenir from a business trip.
why: A colleague gives to me, so the giving comes towards me: くれる.

jp: 先輩[せんぱい]がこの前[まえ]、私[わたし]に試験[しけん]の過去問[かこもん]を{くれました|gv-kureru}。
en: A senior student gave me past exam papers the other day.
why: An older student gives to me; the direction is towards me, so くれる.

jp: 友達[ともだち]が私[わたし]の弟[おとうと]に古[ふる]い教科書[きょうかしょ]を{くれました|gv-kureru}。
en: A friend gave my younger brother an old textbook.
why: The receiver is my brother, on my side, so the giving is くれる.

jp: 同[おな]じクラスの田中[たなか]さんは、いつも私[わたし]にお菓子[かし]を{くれます|gv-kureru}。
en: Tanaka, who is in my class, always gives me sweets.
why: Tanaka gives to me, so くれる; the habit is in the present form.

jp: だれが君[きみ]にこのペンを{くれた|gv-kureru}の？
en: "Who gave you this pen?"
why: The giver is someone else and the receiver is the listener on our side: くれる.

jp: 後輩[こうはい]が私[わたし]に手作[てづく]りのクッキーを{くれました|gv-kureru}。
en: A junior colleague gave me home-made cookies.
why: A junior gives to me and the junior is not honoured, so くれる.

jp: 図書館[としょかん]の人[ひと]が私[わたし]に新[あたら]しいしおりを{くれました|gv-kureru}。
en: The library staff member gave me a new bookmark.
why: The giver is someone else and the receiver is me: くれる.

jp: 私[わたし]は後輩[こうはい]に使[つか]わなくなった参考書[さんこうしょ]を{あげました|gv-ageru}。
en: I gave my junior a reference book I no longer used.
why: I give to someone else, so あげる.

jp: 弟[おとうと]は同級生[どうきゅうせい]に鉛筆[えんぴつ]を{あげました|gv-ageru}。
en: My younger brother gave a classmate a pencil.
why: My brother is on my side and gives outward to a classmate: あげる.

jp: 来月[らいげつ]、お世話[せわ]になった同僚[どうりょう]に小[ちい]さな贈[おく]り物[もの]を{あげます|gv-ageru}。
en: Next month I will give a small present to a colleague who helped me.
why: I give to a colleague, an equal, so あげる.

jp: 母[はは]は隣[となり]の家[いえ]の人[ひと]に畑[はたけ]の野菜[やさい]を{あげました|gv-ageru}。
en: My mother gave vegetables from her field to the neighbour.
why: My mother is on my side and gives outward: あげる.

jp: このボールペン、使[つか]っていいよ。君[きみ]に{あげる|gv-ageru}。
en: "You can use this ballpoint pen. I'll give it to you."
why: The speaker gives to the listener: あげる.

jp: 私[わたし]は留学生[りゅうがくせい]の友達[ともだち]に日本語[にほんご]の絵本[えほん]を{あげました|gv-ageru}。
en: I gave my exchange-student friend a Japanese picture book.
why: I give to a friend, so あげる.

jp: 毎年[まいとし]、私[わたし]は卒業[そつぎょう]する生徒[せいと]に花[はな]を{あげます|gv-ageru}。
en: Every year I (a teacher) give flowers to the students who graduate.
why: The teacher gives to students and they are not honoured: あげる.

jp: 妹[いもうと]は試験[しけん]を受[う]ける友達[ともだち]にお守[まも]りを{あげました|gv-ageru}。
en: My younger sister gave a good-luck charm to a friend who was about to take an exam.
why: My sister is on my side and gives outward to a friend: あげる.

jp: 私[わたし]は友達[ともだち]に宿題[しゅくだい]のプリントを{もらいました|gv-morau}。
en: I got the homework sheet from a friend.
why: I am the receiver and the giver is marked with に: もらう.

jp: 弟[おとうと]は先輩[せんぱい]に古[ふる]いユニフォームを{もらいました|gv-morau}。
en: My younger brother got an old uniform from a senior.
why: The receiver is my brother and the giver is marked with に: もらう.

jp: 私[わたし]は同僚[どうりょう]に使[つか]いやすい手帳[てちょう]を{もらいました|gv-morau}。
en: I received an easy-to-use planner from a colleague.
why: The subject is the receiver, so もらう.

jp: 昨日[きのう]、クラスの友達[ともだち]に面白[おもしろ]い小説[しょうせつ]を{もらいました|gv-morau}。
en: Yesterday I received an interesting novel from a classmate.
why: The subject is the receiver and the giver takes に: もらう.

jp: 私[わたし]は学校[がっこう]の事務[じむ]の人[ひと]に新[あたら]しい学生証[がくせいしょう]を{もらいました|gv-morau}。
en: I got a new student ID card from the school office staff.
why: I am the receiver and the clerk is the giver: もらう.

jp: 妹[いもうと]は図書館[としょかん]の人[ひと]に読書[どくしょ]カードを{もらいました|gv-morau}。
en: My younger sister got a reading card from the library staff.
why: The subject, my sister, receives: もらう.

jp: 山田[やまだ]さんは入社[にゅうしゃ]のお祝[いわ]いに、同期[どうき]から時計[とけい]を{もらいました|gv-morau}。
en: Yamada received a watch from a colleague who joined at the same time, as a gift for joining the company.
why: Yamada is the subject and receives from a peer: もらう.

jp: 私[わたし]は兄[あに]に大学[だいがく]の入学祝[にゅうがくいわ]いを{もらいました|gv-morau}。
en: I received a university-entrance present from my older brother.
why: I am the subject and receive from my brother: もらう.

jp: 私[わたし]は担任[たんにん]の先生[せんせい]に感謝[かんしゃ]の手紙[てがみ]を{さしあげました/あげました|gv-sashiageru}。
en: I gave a thank-you letter to my homeroom teacher.
why: I give to a teacher, so a humble verb for giving is used: さしあげる.

jp: 母[はは]は校長[こうちょう]先生[せんせい]にお菓子[かし]を{さしあげました/あげました|gv-sashiageru}。
en: My mother gave sweets to the principal.
why: My mother is on my side and gives to the honoured principal: さしあげる.

jp: 社長[しゃちょう]に出張[しゅっちょう]のお土産[みやげ]を{さしあげました/あげました|gv-sashiageru}。
en: I gave the company president a souvenir from my business trip.
why: I give to the president, a person to be respected: さしあげる.

jp: 私[わたし]たちはクラス全員[ぜんいん]で書[か]いた色紙[しきし]を先生[せんせい]に{さしあげました/あげました|gv-sashiageru}。
en: As a class we gave our teacher a card we all wrote in.
why: We give to the teacher, so the humble giving verb: さしあげる.

jp: 先生[せんせい]が私[わたし]にこの本[ほん]を{くださいました/くれました|gv-kudasaru}。
en: My teacher gave me this book.
why: A teacher, who is respected, gives to me: くださる.

jp: 社長[しゃちょう]が私[わたし]たちに特別[とくべつ]なボーナスを{くださいました/くれました|gv-kudasaru}。
en: The company president gave us a special bonus.
why: The honoured president gives to us: くださる.

jp: 先生[せんせい]は卒業[そつぎょう]する私[わたし]に、大切[たいせつ]な辞書[じしょ]を{くださいました/くれました|gv-kudasaru}。
en: My teacher gave me a precious dictionary when I graduated.
why: The honoured giver gives to me: くださる.

jp: 部長[ぶちょう]が弟[おとうと]に就職[しゅうしょく]のお祝[いわ]いを{くださいました/くれました|gv-kudasaru}。
en: The department head gave my younger brother a congratulatory gift for his new job.
why: The honoured giver gives to someone on my side: くださる.

jp: 私[わたし]は先生[せんせい]から推薦状[すいせんじょう]を{いただきました/もらいました|gv-itadaku}。
en: I received a letter of recommendation from my teacher.
why: I receive from a teacher, so the humble receiving verb: いただく.

jp: 来週[らいしゅう]、課長[かちょう]から新[あたら]しい仕事[しごと]を{いただきます/もらいます|gv-itadaku}。
en: Next week I will receive a new assignment from the section chief.
why: I receive from a superior, so いただく.

jp: 私[わたし]は取引先[とりひきさき]の社長[しゃちょう]に名刺[めいし]を{いただきました/もらいました|gv-itadaku}。
en: I received a business card from the president of a client company.
why: I receive from an honoured person: いただく.

jp: 私[わたし]は部長[ぶちょう]から会議[かいぎ]の資料[しりょう]を{いただきました/もらいました|gv-itadaku}。
en: I received the meeting materials from the department head.
why: I am the receiver and the giver is a superior: いただく.

jp: 先生[せんせい]に、おいしいお茶[ちゃ]を{いただきました/もらいました|gv-itadaku}。
en: I was given some delicious tea by my teacher.
why: I receive from my teacher: いただく.

jp: 学校[がっこう]のうさぎに、毎日[まいにち]えさを{やります/あげます|gv-yaru}。
en: I give the school rabbits food every day.
why: Giving to an animal uses やる, or あげる in modern speech.
